capabilities.title: Preserve trusted authorship through native dispatch
capabilities.motivation: Native send, queue and restart paths must preserve accepted authors and execution intent while upstream owns scheduling.
behavior: Native send, queue and restart paths must preserve accepted authors and execution intent while upstream owns scheduling.
owners: P6R captures verified actors and native dispatch owns execution and cancellation.

surfaces.summary: Owns DB startup: migrate core, migrate sidecar, then seed personal project; closes DB on failure.

surfaces.summary: Existing send, edit, queue-create, queue-update and compact actions capture native request authorship before accepting content.
surfaces.why: Freeze accepted author/editor evidence from the server request rather than reconstruct it from a later viewer. Admission operation lookup/cancel routes belong to message-acceptance-delivery.

surfaces.summary: Existing create/fork actions pass native request authorship to the thread owner; their201 thread responses remain unchanged.
surfaces.why: Keep initial authorship tied to the originating request through provisioning. This is an authority/capture change, not a separate new identity endpoint.

surfaces.summary: Strict external contribution v1 carries external author and optional integration-asserted person attribution with exact input/operation/thread/mode envelope.
surfaces.why: Retain external-person authorship on accepted/queued messages without conflating it with current authenticated native actor. Contract obligations: personAttribution evidence is integration-asserted; not provider-verified. This is a private protocol reached through externalContributions, not a new REST API. Consumers: apps/server/src/services/p6r/identity-protocol.ts.

surfaces.summary: Specializes the opaque SDK identity boundary into Phosphor session/acceptance/provenance/history/directory/participant models; adds externalContributions {versions:[1],personKinds:[person],history:accepted-and-queued,rollback:requires-capable-host,acceptV1,lookupV1}.
surfaces.why: Keep Phosphor product schema and host-owned effect authorization together while plugins use versioned bb-identity adapters. Contract obligations: These types are NOT exported public Plugin SDK types or REST routes, even though property methods are reachable through the fork-specific opaque capability. Acceptance has submitted/rejected/indeterminate; lookup final/pending/absent-final/unknown; history known/partial/pending/unavailable. Unknown is not empty or safe replay. No claim of compatibility with current upstream or non-fork hosts. Consumers: community-plugins/packages/bb-identity/host-runtime.ts, apps/server/src/services/plugins/plugin-api.ts, apps/server/src/services/p6r/provider-contract.ts.
